pr_title: Use config entry ID as unique ID and remove dependency to getmac in Minecraft Server
pr_body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Currently, the Minecraft Server integration uses following information for creation of unique IDs:
- In case of a SRV record: Host name
- In case of a host name: Host name and port number
- In case of an IP address: MAC address and port number

The last one is causing a lot of troubles for the users, since reading the MAC address via `getmac` has limitations (for example if the HA server and the Minecraft server are in different sub-nets). 

Example: https://community.home-assistant.io/t/can-t-set-up-the-minecraft-server-integration/319547

Additionally using `getmac` for reading MAC addresses for usage in unique IDs is not allowed anymore according to the [development guides](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/config_entries_config_flow_handler#unique-id-requirements):
> Tools that rely on reading the arp cache or local network access such as getmac will not function in all supported network environments and are not acceptable.

Since no unique information is provided by the main dependency `mcstatus`, the config entry ID is the one and only option left. This PR changes the unique ID to the config entry ID. A migration functionality is implemented to migrate the config entry from v1 to v2, so removal and re-adding the integration is not necessary for the user --> No breaking change.

Using the config entry ID as the unique ID has one disadvantage though: Duplicate entries cannot be detected anymore. But in my opinion it is more important that more users can add and use this integration and get less problems during the config flow.

Notes:
- The previous way of generating unique IDs had a bug, which is also fixed by this PR:
  - Entity type _names_ were used as suffix for the  entity unique IDs, which should be entity type _keys_ (Example: `<unique_id>-Protocol version` --> `<unique_id>-protocol_version`).
- After this fix, the one and only helper function in `helpers.py` would only be used by the main class, so I moved the function and removed the empty module.
- I tested this PR with a few servers successfully (more testers are welcome!).

issue_context.title: Running a Minecraft port through a port that is not 25565 is not detected in the initial setup.
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I have a Minecraft server that I changed the port from 25565 to another port in the 50,000's. I thought I could just add it via the integration but I get the following error:

IP address is invalid (MAC address could not be determined). Please correct it and try again.

The IP and port are both correct because I can connect to them on the game using those settings.



### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2023.4.6

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Minecraft Server

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/minecraft_server/
